verdict.rationale: Restate's own docs cover parallel execution and fan-out/fan-in: multiple steps run in parallel, results are combined, and failed branches are retried independently. An orchestrator can dynamically dispatch tasks to workers, and durable sync/async service calls let one handler invoke others. However, this is framed mainly as AI-agent patterns, and the docs never explicitly describe child workflows or fan-out over dynamically sized batches. missing for 10: explicit child/sub-workflow documentation, explicit fan-out/fan-in over dynamic batch sizes in general (non-AI) workflow docs, independent or hands-on corroboration of parallel/fan-in composition.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I compose workflows from parallel steps, fan-out/fan-in over dynamic batches, and child workflows without hand-rolling coordination

citations.quote: Fan out work to multiple agents, then combine the results. Failed agents are retried independently while successful results are preserved.
Execute multiple tool calls in parallel with automatic recovery and coordination.
An orchestrator agent dynamically plans tasks and dispatches them to worker agents. Plans and results are durably persisted.
Call services sync or async with guaranteed execution and exactly-once semantics.
